profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal brainstorming meeting at a large software company between the applied ML research lead for code intelligence and the senior engineer who owns the developer-tooling inference stack. They have both read a recent internal report comparing RAG and fine-tuning for C++ code completion on a 160,000-file WXG codebase, and now need to brainstorm what the next-quarter follow-up should be: a more realistic internal comparative study, a hybrid RAG+FT prototype, or a limited developer pilot. The agenda is to generate candidate experiment ideas, identify what would make the comparison convincing for industrial use, and sketch a lightweight path to try one approach on real C++ repositories. The expected outcome is not a final design, but a shortlist of promising directions and a rough division of follow-up work.

members.name: Linh Zhao
members.role: Applied ML Research Lead, Code Intelligence
members.expertise: Large code models, offline evaluation design, domain adaptation for enterprise code, retrieval-augmented generation
members.background: Linh leads a small research team that reproduced and extended recent LCM studies on the company's internal C++ repositories and has published several internal benchmarking notes used by leadership.
members.private_state: Linh wants a follow-up study that is rigorous, comparable to the previous report, and publishable internally with minimal new platform work; she is wary of getting pulled into deployment-specific integration details too early.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the system must have 'interactive latency', the meaningful number during ideation is model-service time plus retrieval time, not the full editor round-trip.
The 'WXG corpus' naturally refers to the frozen, deduplicated 160,000-file snapshot used in the earlier comparative report, because comparability matters more than freshness at this stage.

In a code-completion study, 'C++ completion' primarily means within-file continuation tasks such as method-body or local-scope next-span prediction, rather than import insertion or cross-file API lookup behavior.
A 'hybrid RAG+FT' setup normally means taking a fine-tuned model and adding retrieval at inference time, since that is the cleanest way to test orthogonality.

members.name: Arjun Menon
members.expertise: IDE integration, low-latency model serving, code indexing, developer telemetry pipelines for C++ tooling
members.background: Arjun owns the internal suggestion service used by several C++ teams in VS Code and CLion, including the code index, request routing, and editor-facing latency dashboards.
members.private_state: Arjun wants any brainstormed idea to be close enough to production reality that it can become a pilot within the quarter; he is trying to avoid adding another fragile online dependency to the tooling stack.
hidden_assumptions: If a proposal mentions 'interactive latency', it must mean keystroke-to-visible-suggestion p95 in the editor, including network hops, retrieval, ranking, and rendering delays.
The 'WXG corpus' means the live mirrored monorepo subset that the indexing service already ingests, because anything else will not reflect current headers, symbols, and internal dependencies.
For developers, 'C++ completion' includes member-access suggestions, include insertion, and cross-file API usage prompts, since those are the completions people actually notice in the IDE.

A practical 'hybrid RAG+FT' should preserve a simple serving path; if retrieval knowledge matters, it is better baked into training examples or an offline reranker than added as another online inference-stage component.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the idea should fit an 'interactive latency' budget.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means service-side latency for retrieval plus generation, measured at the model stack and used for research comparison.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means end-to-end editor latency from keystroke to suggestion display, measured at p95 in the actual IDE flow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both routinely compress several latency notions into the single word 'latency', and in a brainstorming meeting it sounds natural to align on 'interactive' without discussing instrumentation boundaries.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to reusing 'the WXG corpus' or 'the standard snapshot'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the frozen, deduplicated 160,000-file research snapshot from the earlier report.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the live mirrored WXG repositories currently feeding the search index and suggestion service.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is a strong shared institutional shorthand that treats both artifacts as 'the WXG corpus', and each person assumes there is only one obvious version worth discussing.

misalignment_points.topic: What falls under C++ code completion
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want the study to reflect 'real C++ completion' or 'developer-facing completion'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes within-file continuation tasks such as completing function bodies, local control flow, and nearby token spans.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes IDE-visible completions such as member access, namespace/API suggestions, include insertion, and other cross-file assist behaviors.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same mature industry term, and because each works in a different part of the stack, the omitted boundary feels too obvious to state aloud.

misalignment_points.topic: How a hybrid RAG+FT system would be executed
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both endorse trying a 'hybrid RAG+FT' baseline.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 imagines a fine-tuned model that still performs online BM25 or embedding-based retrieval at inference time and consumes retrieved snippets in the prompt.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 imagines using retrieval offline to enrich training data or reranking, then serving the fine-tuned model through the existing single-stage endpoint without live retrieval in the critical path.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At the brainstorming level, 'combine them' sounds fully aligned because both methods are indeed being used; the hidden difference is in where retrieval enters the pipeline, which feels like an implementation detail rather than a separate concept.
